notes: The C registration admits level 1 characters at POS_SLEEPING.
The shared command gate preserves the C POS_SLEEPING entry position.
No argument dispatches to print_group and preserves the exact not-in-group text.
A fresh character with no group receives print_group's exact refusal.
Leading fill words are skipped, so a fill-only argument reaches the no-argument branch.
C one_argument skips leading fill words and ignores trailing words before target lookup.
An unresolved room target emits NOPERSON exactly.
A visible room character who is not the actor's follower receives the C follower refusal.
A character with a master cannot enroll group members.
get_char_room_vis does not resolve an otherwise-online player in another room.
Room lookup reaches a visible NPC before applying the follower gate.
A newly accepted follower receives victim text while the actor and room peers receive their respective Act audiences.
Single-target perform_group changes only the selected victim; group all is the separate self-enrollment path.
The all path groups the actor and eligible followers and preserves actor, victim, and non-victim broadcasts.
print_group renders head and grouped followers with HP, mana, move, level, and class fields.

print_group wraps every stat at C_CMP against the viewer, colours the head row's class abbreviation cyan (line 659) and a follower's green (line 676), and leaves the mobile row uncoloured (line 669); the four-level raw probe pins the C_CMP gate against the C_NRM one the reports use (R1/R2/R5e/R5h).

print_group's head arm has no IS_NPC check (src/act.other.c:651-660), so a grouped mobile leader reports its real stats with CLASS_ABBR's literal "--" (src/utils.h:570), not the dashes row that belongs to a mobile follower (line 669); the invented "Your group leader is not online." is gone. Oracle coverage is not available: the state needs do_group run as a mobile, which C allows through force/order but the port cannot run — group is absent from its mob command surface, where force silently logs and drops unsupported commands. That gap is its own finding, not this row's (R1/R4/R5e/R5h).

print_group resolves the leader by body identity, not by name: C holds ch->master as a live pointer and walks k->followers, so two NPCs sharing a name keep separate follower lists. Two same-named guards with different stats, an unrelated follower on the first and the viewer on the second, pin both halves; a name lookup picked a duplicate at random and merged both follower lists (R1/R3/R5e/R5h).
Kicking clears only AFF_GROUP and emits the exact actor, victim, and room-peer messages.
A kicked follower can be accepted again without changing the follow relation.
When perform_group finds no newly eligible follower, the C already-grouped line is emitted.
A grouped self-target follows the C kick path: victim text goes to the actor and the room receives the non-victim broadcast.
